papers.title: Understanding Non-Split 2-Group Symmetry: (3+1)D SymTFT, Anomaly and Bordism
papers.abstract: We present a systematic study of finite, non-split 2-group symmetries with a non-trivial Postnikov class, focusing on the simplest example with a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 0-form symmetry and a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 1-form symmetry, intertwined together by the non-trivial Postnikov class in $H^3(B\mathbb{Z}_2;\mathbb{Z}_2)\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$, denoted by $\mathcal{G}$. We classify the anomalies of this 2-group symmetry for physical theories in $d$-dimensional spacetime, by computing the oriented bordism groups $\Omega_{d+1}^{\rm SO}(B\mathcal{G})$ and the spin bordism groups $\Omega_{d+1}^{\rm Spin}(B\mathcal{G})$ for $d\leq 5$. For the case of $d=3$, we investigate the Symmetry TFT/TO of the 2-group symmetry $\mathcal{G}$ using the language of fusion 2-categories, as well as (3+1)D TQFT actions, for the cases without or with the 2-group anomaly classified by $\operatorname{Hom}\left(\widetilde{\Omega}_4^{\rm SO}(B\mathcal{G}),U(1)\right) \cong H^4(B\mathcal{G};U(1))\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$. We classify the minimal topological and physical boundary conditions of the Symmetry TFTs, and carry out the categorical Landau paradigm for such a non-split finite 2-group.

papers.title: Finite-size corrections to the crosscap overlap in the two-dimensional Ising model
papers.abstract: We analyze the finite-size corrections to the crosscap overlap in the two-dimensional classical Ising model along its self-dual critical line. Using a fermionic formulation, we express the lattice crosscap overlap in terms of Bogoliubov angles and develop a contour-integral approach by analytically continuing the lattice momentum to the complex plane. This leads to a remarkably simple expression for the crosscap overlap, which demonstrates that the finite-size corrections decay exponentially with system size. We further derive an exact analytical formula for the corresponding decay constant and show that it is determined by the complex singularity structure of the Bogoliubov angle.

papers.title: AlgebrasTQD: Computing Algebras and Interfaces in Twisted Quantum Doubles
papers.abstract: We present AlgebrasTQD, an open-source code written in GAP (Groups, Algorithms, and Programming), for computing condensable algebras and the corresponding topological boundaries and interfaces of twisted quantum doubles $D^\omega(G)$. These algebras can be used to classify 1+1d gapped and gapless phases whose symmetry is related by gauging to a finite group $G$ with anomaly $\omega\in H^3(G,U(1))$, to study 2+1d anyon proliferation and to construct logical gates in non-Abelian topological quantum codes. The functions in AlgebrasTQD compute all condensable algebras $A(H,F,\gamma,\epsilon)$ with their algebra structure and anyons, sort them into isomorphism classes and identify the twin algebras that are inequivalent but share the same anyon decomposition. AlgebrasTQD also determines all the subalgebra relations, the corresponding Hasse diagram and the types of 1+1d phases for any chosen, possibly non-invertible, group-theoretical symmetry. For non-maximal algebras, the code computes the reduced topological order with its $3$-cocycle and the map of anyons across the topological interface. Finally, AlgebrasTQD includes functions that construct certain non-Clifford logical gates via non-Abelian surface codes. We summarize the formulas that are implemented in the AlgebrasTQD code, and we illustrate its use with Abelian and non-Abelian groups including $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ with $\omega_\text{III}$, $D_8$, $A_4$ with and without anomaly, twin algebras and twin phases, and the Clifford-hierarchy gates in quantum doubles of dihedral groups. All arithmetic is exact and AlgebrasTQD can be used with any finite group $G$ and 3-cocycle $\omega$, limited only by the time and size of the calculation. The code is available at https://github.com/AlisonWarman/AlgebrasTQD

papers.title: Twin Algebras: Condensable Algebras beyond Anyons
papers.abstract: Condensable algebras in 2+1d non-chiral topological orders characterize gapped boundary conditions and interfaces. Applied to the Symmetry Topological Field Theory, they allow classification of symmetric gapped phases and impose sharp constraints on possible phase transitions. A condensable algebra is specified not only by its underlying set of anyons, which end on the boundary or interface, but also by its algebra structure. We introduce the concept of twin condensable algebras, which have the same anyon decomposition, but inequivalent algebra structure. We revisit the classification of condensable algebras in $\mathcal{Z}(\text{Vec}_G^\omega)$, i.e. in group-theoretical topological orders for finite groups $G$ with anomaly $\omega$. In this context we are able to identify twin algebras that arise from different mechanisms, such as subgroup data, SPT cocycles, and symmetry actions. In particular, we construct infinite families of examples of twins from so-called Gassmann triples, and exhibit cases in which the reduced topological orders are inequivalent despite having identical anyon content. Physically, twin algebras describe distinct symmetric phases that have isomorphic spaces of ground states, but inequivalent order parameters. Such twin phases never exhibit relative spontaneous symmetry breaking, and can be used to construct phase transitions without hidden symmetry breaking, which are intrinsically beyond Landau transitions.

papers.title: Anisotropic Structural and Magnetic Response in Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$: Al-Sublattice Reconstruction upon Sm Substitution
papers.abstract: Chemical pressure plays a critical role in determining the crystal structures and physical properties of intermetallic compounds. Here, we report the synthesis, crystal structure, and physical properties of Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$, a structural analog of UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$, in which the smaller 5f uranium atoms are replaced by larger 4f samarium atoms. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a tetragonal $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{2}\times1$ superstructure with space group $P\bar{4}2_1m$, derived from a UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$-like average structure with space group $P4_2/nmc$. Comparison with UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$ shows that chemical pressure from U-to-Sm substitution produces a strongly anisotropic structural response rather than a uniform expansion of the Ir-Al framework. While one Ir coordination environment undergoes only modest changes, the other exhibits substantial local rearrangement. The Al sublattice primarily accommodates these structural distortions, with selected Al sites showing positional splitting, anisotropic atomic displacement ellipsoids, and partial occupancies, resulting in an Al-rich composition of approximately Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$. Magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a direction dependence, including a broad anomaly near 50 K for selected magnetic-field orientations. However, the absence of corresponding anomalies in heat capacity, electrical resistivity, and lattice parameters suggests that this feature is more consistent with an anisotropic magnetic crossover than a bulk thermodynamic phase transition. These results highlight how chemical substitution at the f-element site can induce Al-sublattice reconstruction and modify the magnetic response within a closely related Ir-Al structural framework.

papers.title: Where Does the Anion-Redox Hole Go? Reliability of Open-Shell Projection-Based Embedding for Li-Rich Cathodes, from DFT Environments to Quantum Solvers
papers.abstract: Anion redox in Li-rich layered oxides places holes on oxygen next to an antiferromagnetic Mn(IV) d3 lattice, a strongly correlated open-shell problem for which projection-based wavefunction-in-DFT embedding offers a route to correlated and quantum solvers, but whose errors are known mainly for closed-shell molecules. We develop a spin-unrestricted projection-based embedding, exact at the DFT-in-DFT level to the microhartree scale for closed-shell, broken-symmetry and high-spin references with point charges, and apply DMRG-in-DFT to point-charge clusters of delithiated Li(2-x)MnO3, varying the environment functional (0-100% exact exchange), geometry, active region, active-space spin, virtual space, cluster size and magnetic reference. In every setting the lowest SCF state places the hole on an oxygen pair, with no O-O bond. How the hole is shared depends on the functional together with the geometry: hybrids give a full, uncoupled hole at the DFT+U geometry but a partial, weakly covalent hole at their own geometry, a change of up to 0.5 e on one oxygen. Where spin spreads across the active/environment boundary, the integer spin projection of the active space becomes a choice worth up to 0.26 e, and at most 0.09 e once the two Mn neighbors are included. An extended state search found missed lower states for two functionals, changing a pair-oxygen spin by up to 0.45 e. Across all 82 runs the embedded mean field gives the same hole (median DMRG change 0.02-0.04 e); correlation mainly adds O-O covalency. State control and geometry consistency, not the solver, dominate the uncertainty, and total energies are not converged at 30-40 orbitals. For quantum solvers, the embedded Hamiltonian must be spin-unrestricted: a shared-orbital form reverses the hole, while sample-based quantum diagonalization reproduces exact diagonalization, as accurately as, but not better than, classical selected CI.

papers.title: Robustness of Anyonic Time-Domain Interference Against Dephasing
papers.abstract: Recent anyon-collider experiments have identified time-domain braiding (TDB) as a new route to probing anyonic statistics. However, how such time-domain interference responds to environmental noise remains an open question. Here we show that TDB interference is intrinsically more robust than its spatial counterpart. In conventional spatial interference, environmental noise induces phase fluctuations that accumulate throughout all paths, leading to exponential suppression of the interference as the dephasing rate increases. In TDB, by contrast, the interfering temporal paths experience largely overlapping environmental fluctuations, whose contributions cancel out in the relative phase, so that only a small nonoverlapping temporal window contributes to dephasing. As a result, TDB interference decays only algebraically with the dephasing rate, providing a new experimental hallmark for its identification. We propose a Fabry-Perot fractional quantum Hall setup in which both types of interference coexist and experience the same environmental noise, enabling a direct comparison of their dephasing behaviors. Our results establish robustness against dephasing as a fundamental advantage of TDB and suggest new opportunities for exploiting anyonic interference in noisy mesoscopic systems.

papers.title: Symmetry-resolved fermionic correlations in iron-oxide ground spaces
papers.abstract: Symmetries of quantum systems provide a natural way to organize the eigenspaces of many-body Hamiltonians. When degeneracies exist, however, they play a more subtle role as different sets of symmetry operators can resolve the same energy subspace into states with very different correlation properties. We study this interplay using a sequence of FeO and Fe$_2$O$_2$ models. For a Hubbard model of FeO, the ground space is 16-fold degenerate. Resolving it by local magnetizations gives a basis of Slater determinants, while total-spin quantum numbers select entangled and non-Gaussian states from the same ground manifold. Adding density-density Hund interactions breaks the independent spin rotations and reduces the ground space to a spin-reversal pair with maximal magnetization. These states are extremely close to Slater determinants in their natural occupations, yet have finite two-body cumulants and conserved-operator algebras whose orbit dimensions differ substantially from the Slater values. Fe$_2$O$_2$ provides a larger example in which spatial mode entanglement can be substantial while fermionic non-Gaussianity remains weak, with the conserved-operator structure again distinguishing the state from the corresponding Slater transformation class. Together, these examples show that symmetry resolution, mode entanglement, reduced-density-matrix correlations, and conserved-operator structure provide complementary information about interacting and degenerate electronic ground states.

papers.title: Coulomb- and exchange-driven redistribution of spectral correlations
papers.abstract: Electronic correlations reorganize not only the energies of individual electronic states but also the collective structure of the spectrum. Here, first-principles density functional theory calculations combined with random-matrix spectral statistics are used to examine this reorganization in gamma-Ce within a static spin-polarized DFT+U+SOC description. We distinguish the effects of the Coulomb interaction U from those of the exchange interaction J by analyzing nearest-neighbor spacings, reduced spacing ratios, band velocities, and band curvatures across the Ce-4f manifold. Increasing U does not produce a monotonic transition between Poisson- and Wigner-Dyson-like statistics; instead, the region of strongest level repulsion migrates across the 4f manifold as the interaction increases. Exchange produces a qualitatively different response. At fixed U, strongly repulsive and strongly clustered spectral regions coexist within the same 4f manifold even while the total spin moment and 4f occupation remain nearly unchanged. The clustering persists after resolving the spectrum into its dominant j = 5/2 and j = 7/2 components and differs strongly between calculations having the same numerical value of U-J. Within the present DFT+U+SOC description, the spectral response therefore depends on the separate Coulomb and exchange interactions and cannot be represented completely by a single effective U-J parameter. These results show that energy- and character-resolved spectral statistics expose correlation-driven electronic reorganization that is hidden by conventional integrated observables.

papers.title: Three-dimensional quantum Hall insulators in magnetic pyrochlore systems
papers.abstract: We show that a class of pyrochlore materials provides a route to realize 3D Quantum Hall insulators, based on magnetic texture and flat band interference. We study itinerant electrons on a pyrochlore lattice Kondo-coupled to localized moments living on another interpenetrating pyrochlore lattice, with the moments forming a field-selected three-in/one-out texture. The noncoplanar texture generates complex spin-dependent hopping amplitudes and unequal local exchange energies, reconstructing the compact-localized parent flat bands into narrow bands separated by a global three-dimensional gap. The low-energy states are concentrated predominantly on kagome planes within the three-dimensional lattice, reflecting the combined effects of quantum interference and the texture-induced sublattice potential. When the lowest band is fully occupied, the response is characterized by a Chern triplet $\mathbf{C}=(1,1,1)$ and reciprocal Hall vector $\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{H}}=(2\pi/a)(1,1,1)$, giving $\sigma_{yz}=\sigma_{zx}=\sigma_{xy}=e^2/(ha)$. The quantized bulk Hall response enforces chiral surface spectral flow, visible as noncontractible Fermi loops at the surface. Our work opens a new direction in the search for three-dimensional quantum Hall physics in magnetic pyrochlore systems, and suggests a broad design principle based on the interplay of magnetic texture and flat-band interference.

papers.title: Measurement-induced entanglement phases in hyperbolic gauge-Higgs models
papers.abstract: Gauge-Higgs theory in flat spacetime provides a prime theoretical model of multiple phases of matter with distinct entanglement structures. More recently, there has been interest in hyperbolic space and the influence its extensive boundaries have on these structures. Entanglement transitions between non-equilibrium phases, such as topological phases, can be realized by the competition of non-commutating measurements. Here we study the entanglement phases of gauge-Higgs models on hyperbolic lattices described by measurement-only dynamics. We chart 2D phase diagrams by employing topological entanglement entropy and introducing a generalized measurement-induced entanglement tailored for hyperbolic Higgs phases. Utilizing duality, we find a phase absent in Euclidean space, wherein the bulk lattice hosts separated clusters of symmetry-protected topological order. Transitions between this "archipelago" phase and neighboring topological and trivial phases feature a critical exponent $\delta$ belonging to a mean-field universality class. Our essential tool is a 3D resource state inspired by measurement-based quantum computation that simulates the spacetime evolution of the 2D quantum state with a third direction of entanglement. This allows us to analyze spacetime "sponges" of entanglement, which map to classical percolation theory and allow us to infer values of critical points on our phase diagrams' boundaries.

papers.title: Spin-polarized tunneling from a Kondo insulator: equilibrium surface magnetism versus magneto-electric response in SmB$_6$
papers.abstract: We theoretically analyze the spin-polarized tunneling between SmB$_6$ tip and the bicollinear antiferromagnet Fe$_{1+x}$Te. The emergence of magnetic contrast in tunneling requires time-reversal symmetry breaking on the surface of the tip. The magnetic contrast part of the tunneling conductance then has two contributions: the first one originates from the magnetic moment due to the equilibrium long-range order on the surface, while the other is governed by the magnetic moment induced by the electric field of the junction through the surface magneto-electric effect. We show that the ratio of the equilibrium moment to the response extracted near zero bias equals, up to the sign, twice the bias at which the contrast changes sign, independently of the relative strength of the two mechanisms, so that this ratio itself does not measure the strength of the magneto-electric effect. We find that within the experimental energy window $|eV|\lesssim10$~meV the {bias-dependent} field-induced contribution is at most a few percent of the equilibrium one, and the two become comparable only at biases of order $100$~meV or higher. The ratio of the field-induced to the equilibrium contribution is inversely proportional to the distance between the tip and the substrate.

papers.title: Quantum Fisher Information Deficit as a Geometric Signature of Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
papers.abstract: Recently, strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) has been established as a framework for describing quantum phases in open systems. However SW-SSB cannot be characterized by conventional charged two-point correlators. In this work, we show that, for strongly $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric states with local charged involutions, SW-SSB manifests as a persistent deficit from the maximal quantum Fisher information (QFI) under symmetry-neutral pair rotations. A model-independent inequality hierarchy establishes the equivalence of this deficit with fidelity and R\'enyi-1 correlators as asymptotic long-range-order diagnostics. It thereby connects finite-angle state overlaps to a constraint on the infinitesimal Bures geometry along the same pair-generated orbit. For symmetry-projected Gibbs states, we further derive a lower bound on the deficit governed by the mean energy injected by the pair operation. Crucially, locality keeps this energy cost uniformly bounded in system size and endpoint separation, maintaining a finite gap below the maximal QFI at any fixed finite temperature. When ordinary charged long range order is absent, this persistent geometric constraint provides a quantitative information-geometric characterization of thermal SW-SSB.

papers.title: Coulomb Crystallization in Free Electron Beams
papers.abstract: Classical Coulomb crystals and quantum Wigner crystals typically arise when repulsive interactions order like-charged particles in spatially confined environments. Here, we show that transient crystallization can also emerge in freely propagating electron pulses without external trapping. Experimentally, we use a transmission electron microscope to measure number-resolved energy correlations in photoemitted pulses containing up to nine electrons, revealing strong correlations at small particle numbers that progressively disappear in the pulse interior as the number increases. To explain these observations, we combine many-body simulations with a one-dimensional statistical-mechanical model, showing that the leading and trailing electrons generate a self-induced longitudinal potential that transiently confines the inner particles, enabling the formation of an ordered chain during propagation. The resulting crystallization phase diagram reveals how many-body ordering dynamics can be understood in terms of evolving macroscopic beam properties, namely its geometry and the ratio of the mean Coulomb interaction energy to the longitudinal thermal energy. Extending this framework, we theoretically demonstrate that weak transverse guiding through electrostatic or optical ponderomotive forces can sustain crystallization at larger particle numbers and predict spontaneous longitudinal periodic bunching in continuous electron beams. Our results identify conditions under which stochastic Coulomb interactions can be harnessed to generate self-structured, strongly correlated electron beams in both pulsed and continuous regimes.

papers.title: Electronic correlations and dynamical screening with ab initio quantum embedding
papers.abstract: First-principles descriptions of correlated quantum materials require a simultaneous treatment of strong local many-body effects and nonlocal dynamical screening. We present an efficient fully self-consistent implementation of $GW$+EDMFT that combines nonlocal correlations at the $GW$ level with a non-perturbative treatment of local correlations within extended dynamical mean-field theory (EDMFT), with a well-defined double-counting correction and a self-consistently determined impurity interaction. Self-consistency in both the Green's function and the dynamically screened interaction is essential for describing screening processes across energy scales. A key ingredient that makes it computationally feasible is the compression of two-particle correlation functions using interpolative separable density fitting (ISDF). Applying the scheme to the Mott insulator SrMnO$_3$ and the correlated metal LaNiO$_3$, we show that the self-consistent effective local interaction resolves the overscreening inherent to constrained-RPA approaches. For SrMnO$_3$, this stabilizes a Mott-insulating state in quantitative agreement with experiment, while for LaNiO$_3$ local EDMFT corrections yield a quasiparticle mass enhancement consistent with ARPES. These results establish fully self-consistent $GW$+EDMFT as a reliable \emph{ab initio} framework for strongly correlated quantum materials.

papers.title: Revisiting spin Hamiltonian parameters in a Kitaev material via Bayesian optimization of magnetization curves
papers.abstract: Determining the spin Hamiltonian of a magnetic compound is crucial for understanding its magnetic properties. A standard approach is to derive model parameters from ab initio calculations based on the crystal structure. However, the resulting Hamiltonian can depend sensitively on methodological details of the ab initio procedure. This issue is particularly evident in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$, a candidate Kitaev material. Here, we present an alternative, data-driven approach to determine the spin Hamiltonian parameters of $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ by Bayesian optimization of experimental magnetization curves along the $b$- and $c$-axis directions. We optimize five parameters, namely the Kitaev interaction $K$, off-diagonal interactions $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$, the Heisenberg interaction $J$, and the $c$-axis $g$-factor $g_c$. The parameter set that minimizes the cost function is $(K,\Gamma,\Gamma',J,g_c)=(-6.0, 7.5, -0.3, -1.75, 2.3)$, where the exchange couplings are in meV. We find that the cost function is insensitive to the absolute value of the Kitaev coupling $K$. Thus, the magnetization data alone do not determine its energy scale. The cost function also depends only weakly on $\Gamma'$ and $J$, while the optimization favors a large positive $\Gamma$. By computing the static spin structure factor, magnetic susceptibility, and specific heat, we show that these quantities favor the large-$\Gamma$ scenario over the small-$g_c$ scenario and that the parameter set that minimizes the cost function yields good agreement with the experimental structure factor and susceptibility, and qualitative agreement with the specific heat. The combination of Bayesian optimization and accurate low-energy solvers provides an effective approach for determining parameters of spin Hamiltonians. This methodology opens a systematic route to determining spin Hamiltonians in quantum magnets from experimental data.

papers.title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
papers.abstract: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At $1/8$ doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform $d$-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-$t$ energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.

papers.title: Same-spin correlation screens the exchange peak of the electron gas near 2kF
papers.abstract: Exchange alone gives the electron gas a local field factor with a sharp peak just below 2kF. Quantum Monte Carlo finds none. Both spin channels are computed here from their lowest diagrams with a dynamically screened interaction and no fitting. Parallel spin correlation is the negative image of exchange and removes about half the peak; the calculated spin-resolved factors account for the QMC data at rs = 1 and 2, and at q = 0 for the compressibility and spin susceptibility obtained from the ground-state energy. The two classes of diagrams are the two terms of the kernel of Hedin's vertex equation, of which the second is routinely dropped.

papers.title: An exactly solvable obstructed seam on a lattice Klein bottle: bulk-locked Majorana rings and register-dependent toric codes
papers.abstract: We study a frustrated seam produced by literal reflection gluing of Wen's plaquette model on a closed lattice Klein bottle. The seam operators anticommute along two cycles for even circumference and one cycle of twice the length for odd circumference. Their algebra reduces to free Majorana rings, while the commuting bulk stabilizers constrain the allowed ring sectors. This bulk locking yields exact ground energies, excitation gaps and degeneracies, checked by phase-aware Pauli traces and finite-size diagonalization, including two 24-qubit energy predictions. The seam degeneracy is not topological: the single-site seam fields tested split it at second order. We contrast this obstructed gluing with consistent toric-code realizations. An edge register preserves the anyon labels; a Hadamard-dressed site register has colour-dependent seam transport, with ground-state degeneracy 2 or 4 for even circumference and a sign-frustrated exception at odd circumference. For the enumerated lattice isometries and sizes, we compute logical gates and distances, distinguishing abstract qubit relabelling from local hardware depth. Finally, on three 16- and 24-qubit lattices, chiral matter selects a holonomy doublet whose electric-field splitting follows two competing tunnelling routes. These matter results remain finite-size statements. The main result is the exact obstructed-seam solution with bulk sector locking; the register, gate and matter calculations delimit its relation to topological codes.

papers.title: Agentic Swarms Discover Enhanchment of Fractional Chern Insulator Gaps Beyond Ideal Quantum Geometry
papers.abstract: Can artificial intelligence (AI) move beyond solving well-defined problems to contribute to open-ended discovery in fundamental physics? Could AI propose what to explore, identify unexpected phenomena, and uncover their mechanisms? We address this using MOSAIC (Multi-agent Open-ended Scientific Analysis and Investigation through Collaboration), a collaborative swarm of AI agents (Claude Opus 5.5), to tackle a longstanding bottleneck: the small energy gaps limiting the robustness of fractional topological order and the study of anyons at higher temperatures. Rather than prescribing a model, we ask frontier models (GPT-6 Astra) to propose a theoretical framework, which MOSAIC explores through diverse strategies and rapid exchange of ideas. This reveals a striking finding: although ideal quantum geometry is considered favorable for fractional states, departing from this limit can dramatically enhance their robustness, with many-body gaps more than an order of magnitude larger than in the ideal case. Without centralized coordination, the agents explored autonomously, combined findings across agents, and formed insights from individual runs, outperforming isolated agents with the same tools. AI-assisted theoretical analysis further develops simplified models with an analytical gap enhancement factor that is unbounded within the single-band approximation. Remarkably, AI identifies the real-space quantum metric, rather than the momentum-space one, as the key quantity governing the many-body gap, revealing how flat-band wavefunctions shape two-electron interactions and yielding an index computable from single-particle wavefunctions without many-body ED to guide gap optimization. Our study demonstrates how collaborative AI agents can integrate exploration, discovery of unexpected physics, and theoretical understanding, opening new possibilities for AI-driven research in fundamental physics.

papers.title: Planckian dissipation per unit critical entropy as a coupling-free probe of the strange-metal bath
papers.abstract: Strange metals pair a resistivity linear in temperature with a specific heat $C/T$ rising logarithmically on cooling. We find that, if electrons scatter off a local critical bath, the coupling cancels in the ratio $Q$ of their coefficients, leaving two measurable numbers: how slowly the bath relaxes, seen in photoemission or optics, and the share of critical entropy that relaxes current. Baths form classes: $Q\le4.91$ for a conformal bath, as SYK models confirm; 9--15 for the Yukawa--SYK field; and far less for Kondo lattices. LSCO, at $Q\approx9$, exceeds the conformal bound, pointing to the Yukawa--SYK field.

papers.title: Mesons, Confinement, and Complexity: A Krylov Space Perspective on the Long-Range Ising Chain
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay between confinement and Krylov complexity in the long-range transverse-field Ising chain, where power-law interactions $\sim 1/r^{\alpha}$ generate an effective confining potential between domain walls without an explicit symmetry-breaking field. Using the time-averaged Krylov state complexity after a quench as a diagnostic, we find that the complexity is strongly suppressed and only weakly system size-dependent at small $\alpha$ and small transverse field $h_x$, where confinement is strongest, and crosses over to rapid growth at larger $\alpha$, where it increases with system size. Within the confined regime, the oscillation frequencies of the complexity agree with the meson masses of an effective two-kink model, with the dominant frequency growing linearly with the lightest meson mass and the time-averaged complexity decreasing approximately as its inverse square. We further study operator Krylov complexity at finite temperature using the Wightman inner product. At low temperature, it exhibits bounded oscillations that directly encode the meson spectrum, whereas this structure is progressively washed out as the temperature increases. These results identify Krylov complexity as a spectroscopic probe of interaction-induced confinement and reproduce, in a microscopic lattice model, the hallmarks of Krylov complexity identified in confining field theories.

papers.title: A cascade of orbital-field-driven phases with a Lifshitz-type transition to unidirectional spiral order
papers.abstract: Frustration in magnetic systems gives rise to unconventional orders and exotic spin liquids. Here, we explore a new type of frustration arising from an intrinsic bond-dependent orbital-field that couples orbital degrees of freedom to spin correlations. Introducing this orbital-field interaction into the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice, we show that local spin-orbital constraints generate a subextensive degeneracy, lifted by order-by-disorder to select distinct collinear magnets in a cascade of phases as the orbital field increases from a para-orbital liquid. At larger fields, the selected phase gives way to an incommensurate unidirectional spiral that spontaneously breaks chiral symmetry. This transition is driven by the coupling of a Goldstone mode to gapped dynamical spin-orbital fluctuations. The spin stiffness becomes negative along a particular direction, while the spiral wavevector grows as the square root of the distance from the transition, signaling a Lifshitz-type transition. We present a microscopic route to realizing this orbital field and discuss candidate materials.

papers.title: Towards Quantum Computation of Bulk FeO
papers.abstract: Quantum computation offers a promising path towards efficient calculations of the electronic structure of correlated materials. The properties of iron-based materials, which are key for advancing geological and astrophysical understanding, are notoriously difficult to calculate with classical computers. However, despite the many recent advances in quantum computing on near intermediate scale quantum hardware, a full treatment of the electronic structure of high-$Z$ atoms or molecules remains challenging. Here, we investigate the ground-state properties of molecular FeO and Fe$_2$O$_2$ model Hamiltonians using classical exact diagonalization, Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), and Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD). The experimental quintet ground state of FeO is recovered classically and with quantum algorithms, while a nonet ground state is recovered for Fe$_2$O$_2$. Although raw VQE does not achieve chemical accuracy for the ground state of FeO or Fe$_2$O$_2$, SQD with two connectivity shells recovers the exact ground energy for both molecules utilizing remarkably few quantum computational resources. Overall, our results indicate that $ab \; initio$-informed low-energy models of correlated materials, combined with SQD, offer a new alternative for scaling up calculations of ground-state properties of strongly correlated solids on existing quantum hardware.

papers.title: Large superconducting diode effect indicates nonuniform triplet pairing in UTe2
papers.abstract: The superconducting diode effect (SDE) is characterized by unequal critical current magnitudes for opposite-polarity current flow, owing to broken spatial-inversion and time-reversal symmetries. For a superconducting pair wavefunction to spontaneously break inversion symmetry implies the formation of Cooper pairs with nonzero momentum, yielding a nonuniform superconducting state. For singlet superconductors, the formation of such a (FFLO) state has long been understood to provide an escape from high field Pauli pair-breaking -- how and why such an effect might occur for equal spin pairing is an open question. Here we report the observation of a large SDE in bulk specimens of the three-dimensional heavy-fermion triplet superconductor UTe$_2$, with a peak diode efficiency of 33% at the high magnetic field strength of 33.6 T, representing the highest-field observation of the SDE to date. Crucially, this nonreciprocal transport is strictly confined to a narrow field regime where superconductivity coexists with a field-induced spin-polarized state near a first-order metamagnetic phase boundary. The absence of the SDE away from this slender phase-intersection argues strongly against purely extrinsic vortex pinning asymmetries. Instead, our findings indicate spontaneous inversion symmetry breaking accompanied by finite-momentum Cooper pairing. We model this behavior using a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau theory, demonstrating that the intertwining of magnetic and triplet superconducting orders can stabilize an odd-parity FFLO state.

papers.title: Vortex anisotropy in chiral and nematic superconductors with strain
papers.abstract: Unconventional superconductors with a two-component order parameter support the existence of a rotational symmetry breaking nematic phase and a time-reversal symmetry breaking chiral phase. A recent experiment on 4Hb-TaS$_2$ surprisingly shows both twofold anisotropy in $H_{c2}$, which suggests nematic superconductivity, as well as isotropic vortices at low temperatures, which suggest chiral superconductivity. To resolve this apparent conundrum we write down the appropriate Ginzburg-Landau equations and develop a numerically efficient algorithm for finding vortex solutions, allowing us to study their shape and anisotropy over a broad parameter range. We also demonstrate analytically that, to leading order, the vortex anisotropy is independent of strain in the nematic case, but is linearly dependent on it in the chiral phase, providing a possible way to distinguish the two phases. Using all these results we show that, in the presence of strain, in a large parameter regime the system behaves nematically near the transition, leading to an anisotropy of $H_{c2}$, but is dominantly chiral away from the transition, leading to parametrically smaller vortex anisotropy, in line with the experiment.

papers.title: Continuum neural wavefunctions for anyons on a torus
papers.abstract: Mobile anyons in topologically ordered phases provide a setting to investigate how fractional exchange statistics shapes collective behavior at finite density. We introduce AnyFormer: a neural variational framework for continuum anyons on a torus that explicitly incorporates statistical interactions and global winding constraints. We construct a smooth orbital frame that enforces the matrix-valued torus boundary conditions, and supplement it with an analytic pair factor that supplies the regular collision behavior. The orbital geometry and many-body amplitudes are optimized in parallel by variational Monte Carlo. We apply AnyFormer to semions without an external field or interaction potential, isolating unique correlations generated solely by statistics. Our framework closely matches exact two-semion energies and yields lower variational energies than finite-cutoff exact diagonalization for $N = 4$ and $6$ semions. Scaling up to $N = 16$ semions, well beyond the limits of continuum diagonalization, our calculations reveal states with pronounced correlation holes, suppressed long-wavelength density fluctuations, and a reversal of pair circulation at a distance set by the mean particle spacing. For $N = 12$ and $16$ semions, the circulation develops damped spatial oscillations. AnyFormer thus provides a scalable variational neural-net framework for microscopic studies of correlations, chiral motion, and collective phases of bulk anyonic matter.

papers.title: Ground-State Properties of a Lattice-Coupled Strongly Correlated Model for Solid Oxygen under Pressure
papers.abstract: Solid oxygen is an $S=1$ molecular magnet with strong coupling between spin and lattice degrees of freedom. Recent studies suggest that magnetic moments coexist with tetramer distortions under pressure. We derive an effective spin Hamiltonian from a two-orbital Peierls--Hubbard model with spin-orbit coupling. The resulting model contains competing easy-plane single-ion and easy-axis exchange anisotropies. We analyze this model on a square lattice using quantum Monte Carlo simulations and evaluate the magnetic contribution to the lattice stiffness for several lattice distortion patterns including the tetramer pattern. We find that the tetramer pattern is the most favorable among the considered distortion patterns throughout the parameter range studied. Moreover, competition between the two anisotropies enhances the tendency toward lattice distortion and strengthens the preference for tetramerization over the other patterns.

papers.title: Magnon Super-Bloch Oscillations and Switchable Transport in Driven Magnonic Crystals
papers.abstract: Super-Bloch oscillations (SBOs) offer a powerful route to control wave packet propagation in driven lattices, yet their realization in magnonic systems has remained elusive. Here, we predict SBOs of magnon wave packets in periodic magnonic crystals driven by static and ac gradients of magnetic anisotropy field. A static gradient alone induces magnon Bloch oscillation (BO) with a constant carrier frequency. Remarkably, adding a near-resonant MHz-scale ac driving gives rise to a slow large-amplitude envelope oscillation, the hallmark of SBO. At exact resonance, the ac driving enables phase-controlled directional transport with a carrier-frequency shift up to GHz scale. Consequently, the same structure can be switched among three distinct regimes: conventional BO, SBO, and directed transport. Analytical expressions for the oscillation amplitudes, superperiod, drift velocity, and frequency evolution are validated by micromagnetic simulations. Extending to antiferromagnet magnonic crystals, we further demonstrate that these effects drive opposite motions of two oppositely polarized magnon modes in THz range. Our work establishes magnon SBOs as a versatile platform, opening a new avenue for reconfigurable magnonic devices.

papers.title: Stripe antiferromagnetic order and spin dynamics in the Shastry-Sutherland Ising compound Er2Be2GeO7
papers.abstract: In rare-earth compounds, the interplay between geometric frustration and unusual single-ion anisotropy caused by the crystal electric field often leads to exotic magnetic phases. Here, we investigate the magnetic properties of the rare-earth Shastry-Sutherland compound Er$_2$Be$_2$GeO$_7$ using bulk measurements and neutron scattering down to sub-Kelvin temperatures. A $k=(0,0,0)$ stripe-like antiferromagnetic order with locally tilted Er$^{3+}$ moments is revealed by time-of-flight neutron powder diffraction, accompanied with a $\lambda$-shape specific-heat anomaly at $T_N=0.84$ K. The temperature dependence of the magnetic peak intensity corresponding to the ordered moment of Er$^{3+}$ approximates to the two-dimensional Ising universality class. Thermal- and cold-neutron inelastic scattering experiments demonstrate that the strong Ising anisotropy originates from the local crystal electric field, and reveal gapped magnetic excitations with weak dispersion in the ordered state. Mean-field random-phase approximation with inequivalent nearest-neighbor couplings accounts well for the collective excitations, while classical Monte Carlo simulations yield the fractional $1/4$ and $1/2$ magnetization plateaus. Our work provides a comprehensive description of the spin correlations in Er$_2$Be$_2$GeO$_7$ with a particular focus on the classical origin of its fractional magnetization plateaus.
